behaviors.source: GH #84 What to build; prd.md D1 ownership table
behaviors.when: Object.keys of that namespace is sorted

behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts the sorted keys deep-equal that six-name list, so an extra or missing runtime export fails; pnpm run typecheck accepts the pinned signatures and types

behaviors.source: GH #84 What to build (pure validator); prd.md D1 example JSON
behaviors.given: prd.md D1's fully populated example policy, already parsed
behaviors.when: parseGatePolicy(policy) is called with no filesystem access
behaviors.then: it returns a GatePolicy with version 1, gatePolicyPaths [afk.config.json, suite-budgets.json], testGlobs [**/*.test.ts] and all three risk classes
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts the result deep-equals that policy, pinning the validator's success path

behaviors.given: four reduced policies: {version:1}, one without protectedPaths, one without riskClasses, one whose protectedPaths omits testGlobs
behaviors.then: each parses and the omitted members return the documented baselines: [afk.config.json, suite-budgets.json], [**/*.test.ts], and all three risk classes
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts each result deep-equals the baseline-filled policy, and that mutating a returned array leaves the DEFAULT_ constants unchanged

behaviors.given: malformed inputs: null; "policy"; protectedPaths as []; protectedPaths as a string; gatePolicyPaths as [7]; riskClasses as {}
behaviors.then: each throws an Error naming the offending key rather than returning a partial policy
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts the six calls reject with messages matching /protectedPaths/, /gatePolicyPaths/ or /riskClasses/ as applicable

behaviors.source: GH #84 AC2; prd.md D1 unknown-member rule
behaviors.given: a valid policy extended once each with the unknown top-level keys cost, acceptance and typo, and once with the unknown protectedPaths member testGlob
behaviors.then: each throws an Error naming that exact member, so a key #85 or #86 has not landed yet is never silently ignored
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts the four rejection messages contain cost, acceptance, typo and testGlob respectively

behaviors.source: GH #84 AC3 and its independent-version note
behaviors.given: policies whose version is absent, 2, and "1"; plus a temp-directory afk.config.json whose top-level version is 1 while gatePolicy.version is 2
behaviors.when: the first three go to parseGatePolicy and the fourth is read by loadGatePolicy
behaviors.then: all four are refused with an Error naming version, proving gatePolicy.version is checked independently of the file's own top-level version
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts four rejections matching /version/, the last from loadGatePolicy against a file whose top-level version is valid

behaviors.source: GH #84 AC6; prd.md D1 and D5's three classes
behaviors.given: policies whose riskClasses are [gate-policy, gatePolicy] and [deleted-tests]
behaviors.then: each throws at parse time naming the unrecognised string gatePolicy or deleted-tests
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts each message contains the offending literal, and GATE_RISK_CLASSES holds exactly the three declared classes

behaviors.given: four mkdtempSync directories: one whose afk.config.json carries a well-formed gatePolicy; one with no afk.config.json; one whose config has no gatePolicy key; one whose gatePolicy has an unknown member
behaviors.then: the first returns the policy deep-equal to what was written, the second and third return null, the fourth throws naming the member
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts all four outcomes, so an implementation that always returns null fails case one

behaviors.given: glob **/*.test.ts against src/deep/nested/a.test.ts, a.test.ts, src/gate-policy.ts and src\\deep\\a.test.ts; glob src/*.test.ts against src/a.test.ts and src/deep/a.test.ts
behaviors.when: matchesGlob(glob, path) is called on each pair
behaviors.then: ** spans zero or more segments so both test paths match; the non-test path does not; the backslash path matches because the path is normalized to forward slashes first; * does not cross a segment, so src/deep/a.test.ts fails src/*.test.ts
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts true, true, false, true for the first glob and true, false for the second

behaviors.source: prd.md D6 case rule; anchors/01-gate-policy-reader.md Do not conflate two case rules
behaviors.given: glob **/*.test.ts against src/a.Test.ts and SRC/a.test.ts; glob src/Gate.ts against src/gate.ts
behaviors.when: matchesGlob runs on each pair on the current platform, Windows included
behaviors.then: a path differing from a literal only in case does not match: .Test.ts fails and src/gate.ts fails, while SRC/a.test.ts matches because ** absorbs SRC and no literal is compared there
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts false, true, false for those pairs and reads src/gate-policy.ts to assert no toLowerCase and no toUpperCase call, so the rule cannot become platform-dependent

behaviors.source: GH #84 AC10; prd.md D6 (any other metacharacter refuses the launch and names the character)
behaviors.given: one glob per rejected metacharacter of the enumerated set — src/?.ts, src/[ab].ts, src/a].ts, src/{a,b}.ts, src/a}.ts, src/(a).ts, src/a).ts, src/!a.ts, src/a+.ts, src/a@.ts, src\\a.ts — plus src/***.ts and a**/b.ts, where ** is not the whole segment
behaviors.when: each is passed as the glob argument to matchesGlob, and separately as a testGlobs member to parseGatePolicy
behaviors.then: every call throws an Error naming what it rejected: the character for the eleven metacharacters, the segment for the two malformed-star globs; both entry points share one validator and refuse identically
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts asserts each glob rejects from both matchesGlob and parseGatePolicy with a message containing that character or segment; the backslash case pins the pair against B-09, where a backslash in a path is normalized
